name: An Executable Benchmark of LLM-Assisted Database Administration Across Task Difficulty: Correctness, Repair, and Cost
description: This is a confirmatory computational empirical benchmark of LLM-assisted database administration across task difficulty. The study evaluates two pre-frozen checkpoints on project-generated, non-sensitive synthetic SQL/configuration tasks spanning five task families and three structural-complexity tiers. The primary unit is one model × task × seed trajectory. Confirmatory questions test whether structural complexity predicts first-attempt executable success (H1) and whether complexity slopes differ between checkpoints (H2). A secondary analysis evaluates bounded repair with answer-free verifier feedback within at most three attempts (H3). No human participants or identifiable data are involved; outcomes are executable correctness, repair, latency, token and cost measures under the frozen protocol.
